audit_result.proof_trace: The property requires Zod safeParse before every DB mutation, but six exported Server Actions bypass it entirely: toggleAdminStatus, deleteMember, updateMemberTeams, updateStatusesForNewAcademicYear (members.ts), and deleteTeam, updateTeamLeaders (teams.ts) all perform DB writes with raw string/number/array parameters. The most impactful is updateStatusesForNewAcademicYear (L624-703), which accepts an unvalidated integer that drives bulk status reassignment of all members via generation arithmetic — only a basic >0 check is present, no Zod schema enforcing range or type constraints. All violating functions are admin-gated and Supabase uses parameterized queries, limiting practical exploitability to admin account compromise scenarios.
audit_result.attack_scenario: A compromised admin account (e.g., via Discord OAuth session hijack) invokes updateStatusesForNewAcademicYear with a crafted generation value (e.g., extremely large integer), corrupting the status field for all non-deleted members in bulk; alternatively, updateMemberTeams is called with an oversized teamIds array causing excessive DB inserts, both bypassing any Zod-enforced constraints.

PROP-stem-system-pre-012.text: All form inputs must be validated via Zod schema (safeParse) before any DB mutation.
